links.outcome: Fully-correct response rate of LLMs on real patient multi-turn questions versus physician ground truth
links.effect: Even the strongest model, GPT-5, achieved only 41.2% fully-correct responses; all five models degraded significantly from turn 0 to turn 2 (p < 0.001).
links.quote: Even the strongest model, GPT-5, achieves only 41.2% fully-correct responses.

links.outcome: Multi-turn consistency and error propagation across conversation turns
links.effect: Wrong-answer rates roughly tripled by turn 2; a single wrong turn raised the probability of a subsequent wrong turn by 1.9-6.1x; nearly one in three Claude Haiku conversations swung between fully correct and completely wrong.
links.quote: EPR shows that a single wrong turn raises the probability of a subsequent wrong turn by 1.9-6.1x across all models.

screen.reason: Empirical benchmarking paper assessing multi-turn medical QA dialogue performance and error propagation across five commercial LLMs using real patient-physician online consultation threads.
